clue.text: Dance seen in pantomime Our Gang orchestrated originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A dance number in a pantomime, scored for the Our Gang children's comedy troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Our Gang was the Hal Roach children's comedy series of the silent era, one of the puzzle's many silent-film names.
explanation.definitionFit: The pogo is a punk-era dance where people jump straight up and down on the spot.

clue.text: Was absent, yet recast? Not Stan Laurel

indicators.note: to recast is to put into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
Not says the letters of the following name are excluded from the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; Stan Laurel was the thin half of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Someone who was missing gets recast, so the part goes to anyone but Stan Laurel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of WAS ABSENT YET, remove S, T, A, N (Stan), and rearrange what is left. 'Laurel' looks like part of the name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet bay is the bay laurel tree, whose leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Communist trap? On the contrary, not Hardy

indicators.note: on the contrary means the opposite way round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a communist is a Red
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A trap set by a communist, or the other way round, with no part for Oliver Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: RED and NET together read backwards give the answer. 'Hardy' looks like Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy, but here it is the gardener's word for a plant that survives frost.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender plant cannot survive frost, the opposite of a hardy one.

clue.text: Hapless Chase met agents to make cuts

indicators.note: hapless means unlucky or in a sorry state, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Unlucky Chase meets agents who are there to make cuts, like a studio budget review.
explanation.walkthrough: Charley Chase was a silent-film comedian, so 'Hapless Chase' reads as a person. Rearrange CHASE MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Machetes are broad heavy blades, the tools you use for hacking through vegetation.

clue.text: Buster Keaton missing on second shooting of scene!

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning

indicators.note: a buster breaks things apart, so the name's remaining letters are smashed into a new order
missing says the short word is taken away from the name

explanation.surface: Buster Keaton isn't there, so the scene has to be shot a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes ON from Keaton, leaving KEAT, which 'Buster' scrambles. The blog instead splits 'Buster' into 'Bust' (the anagram signal) plus 'er', which joins the fodder; both readings make the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retake is a repeat filming of a shot or scene that was not good enough the first time.

clue.text: Funny film shortened — would be, too, if the ending was cut

definitions.text: Funny film shortened — would be, too, if the ending was cut

parts.words: Funny film shortened — would be, too, if the ending was cut
parts.note: a funny animated film is named by the clipped informal word for it; chop off that word's final letter and the word too remains, echoing the clue

explanation.surface: A comedy short gets trimmed, and it would end up too short if the ending was cut as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Two hints: a shortened word for a cartoon, and a playful note that cutting its last letter leaves TOO, which echoes 'too' in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Toon is the informal short form of cartoon, an animated funny film.

clue.text: Don't split small dead plant

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all and not split or share it
wee is Scottish and informal for small
d is the standard abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Advice not to divide a small dead plant when you repot it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogweed is a tall umbellifer weed of hedgerows and roadsides; giant hogweed burns the skin.

clue.text: Removing wrappers to use gas oven, Lloyd prepared food

indicators.note: removing the wrappers of each word strips its outer letters, leaving the insides of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Harold Lloyd unwraps a meal and uses the gas oven to cook it.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Lloyd was a silent-film comedian famous for hanging from a clock. A saveloy is a British seasoned pork sausage, usually sold ready cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a precooked smoked sausage, sold ready to eat in chip shops.

clue.text: Keystone Cops' initial material, worth mining

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here taken from the possessive

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal or mineral worth extracting

explanation.surface: The Keystone Cops' earliest footage is a rich seam worth digging into.
explanation.walkthrough: The Keystone Cops were Mack Sennett's bumbling silent-film policemen, so 'Keystone Cops' reads as one name; here 'Keystone' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central principle that everything else depends on, the heart of a matter.

clue.text: Director mistakenly cut Roach's last saloon number in storage on farm

indicators.note: mistakenly means done wrongly, so these letters come out in the wrong order
last points to the final letter of the producer's name

parts.note: a saloon is a bar
N is the abbreviation for number, as in algebra

explanation.surface: A director wrongly cuts Hal Roach's final saloon number from a silent picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Hal Roach was the producer behind Laurel and Hardy. 'number' looks like a musical number but is just N.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is an open-sided farm building with a curved roof, used for keeping hay.

clue.text: For some, WC Fields blowing his top with hate is outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous behaviour is wild, so these letters run riot into a new order
blowing his top means losing the head, so the first letter is cut from the name

explanation.surface: W.C. Fields loses his temper, and his hatred is outrageous to some.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields was the bulbous-nosed comedian, so 'WC Fields' reads as one name; split it, 'WC' (toilet) joins the definition. Removing F leaves IELDS; rearrange it with HATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is the women's public toilet, which some people would call a WC.

clue.text: Keep out of steep enclosure for entry to barbican

indicators.note: enclosure for says the first piece wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: steep in the sense of expensive means dear

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A steep walled enclosure guards the way into a castle's barbican.
explanation.walkthrough: A barbican is an outer defensive gateway of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to bar or exclude someone from a place or right.

clue.text: Langdon's heart captured by desperate lament

indicators.note: captured by says the letter is held inside the word that follows

parts.note: a desperate situation is dire

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Silent comic Harry Langdon's core is caught up in a desperate lament.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Langdon was a baby-faced silent-film comedian; his name has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, G.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, a lament.

clue.text: In every other Sennett reel, artist begs

indicators.note: every other picks alternate letters, here the second, fourth and so on across the three words

explanation.surface: An artist pleads for a part in each alternate Mack Sennett film reel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mack Sennett founded Keystone Studios. Starting from the second letter, take every other letter of SENNETT REEL ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead earnestly, so entreats is a synonym for begs.

clue.text: Quite forgetting to count

indicators.note: forgetting says the following short word is left out of the longer one

parts.note: quite in its sense of completely means totally

explanation.surface: Someone loses track and quite forgets how to count.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running count or record of a score, or the verb to reckon up.

clue.text: Clamour for return of Fatty Arbuckle in small part

indicators.note: return means a going back, so the letters run backwards
in small part says only a short stretch inside these words is used

explanation.surface: Fans clamour for the comeback of Fatty Arbuckle, even in a bit part.
explanation.walkthrough: Roscoe 'Fatty' Arbuckle was a silent-film star. The run YARB inside FATTY ARBUCKLE, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bray is to make a loud harsh noise, like a donkey, which is a raucous clamour.

clue.text: Poach cycling ducks

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter round to the back of the word

parts.note: to poach is to steal, as with a rival's staff

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to poach ducks while riding a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poach' looks like a cooking instruction but means to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Teals are small freshwater dabbling ducks.

clue.text: Silent comic ain't curt

indicators.note: something comic is ludicrous or jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A silent-film comedian isn't brusque, just wordless.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn describes someone who says little, reserved in speech.

clue.text: See 22
Clue to warming together

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction, an arm placed inside another word for arm, wing: W(ARM)ING makes this word

explanation.surface: A hint about warming up together.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the instruction that builds 'warming'. ARM goes inside WING (a bird's arm).
explanation.definitionFit: To walk arm in arm is to go side by side with arms linked, closely together.

clue.text: He went from Italy to America by scooter to join fashion house, squandering silver

definitions.text: He went from Italy to America

indicators.note: squandering means losing or wasting, so these letters are thrown out of the joined words

parts.note: a Vespa is the classic Italian motor scooter
Gucci is an Italian fashion house
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An Italian emigrant rides a scooter to work at a fashion house but blows his money.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of silver's symbol are lost one from each brand. Amerigo Vespucci was the Florentine explorer after whom America is named.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci was an Italian navigator who sailed to the New World, which bears his name.

clue.text: Old Russian clown is said to die

indicators.note: is said says the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Oleg Popov was a famous Soviet circus clown

explanation.surface: An old Russian clown is reported to have died.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop off is informal slang meaning to die suddenly.

clue.text: Boatman's following silent film, a universal horror

indicators.note: following says the setter's word comes after the word for silent

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
the setter Boatman refers to himself, so Boatman's means my

explanation.surface: Boatman follows silent cinema with a universal horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'universal' hints at Universal Pictures, the studio behind the classic horror films, including The Mummy (1932).
explanation.definitionFit: The Mummy is a Universal Studios horror movie starring Boris Karloff as a revived Egyptian corpse.

clue.text: Coarse grass laid down and shooting up

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same written downwards as upwards, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: the wordplay is the answer itself, the grass name, which reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Coarse grass that's been laid down as turf and is already shooting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid down' and 'shooting up' sound like growing grass, but they say the word reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a tough coastal grass planted to bind sand dunes.

clue.text: Drunken parties with pineapple and edam starters as canapé

indicators.note: drunken means unsteady and reeling, so these letters stagger into a new order
starters points to the opening letter of each of the two foods

explanation.surface: Boozy parties serving pineapple-and-edam starters on sticks as canapés.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange PARTIES with P and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served before a meal, a kind of appetiser.

clue.text: Boatman has appeal but not much

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, a man of boats
it is informal for sex appeal

explanation.surface: The setter Boatman admits he has charm, but not a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boatman' looks like the setter's self-reference, but here it is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit means a little or slightly, a small amount.

clue.text: Normand — one in supporting role as a rule

parts.note: the name reads as Norm and, so it gives the man's name Norm with and acting as the link
an ally is someone who supports you

explanation.surface: Mabel Normand, as a rule, was cast in a supporting role.
explanation.walkthrough: Mabel Normand was a Keystone comedy star. Split her surname as 'Norm and' to get NORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means usually, under ordinary circumstances.

clue.text: Garvin finally accepted in routine, the smallest of the brood

indicators.note: accepted in says the letter is taken inside the word that follows

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the actress's name

explanation.surface: Comic actress Anita Garvin finally slots into a routine with the brood's smallest.
explanation.walkthrough: Anita Garvin was a Hal Roach comedienne who worked with Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest, weakest animal in a litter.

clue.text: Athletic Chaplin for head of Disney!

parts.note: the name splits as Chap and LIN: Athletic Chap is the definition, and the remaining LIN is used as letters

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Charlie Chaplin puts on a sporty turn for Walt Disney.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is really 'Athletic Chap': Linford Christie, the British Olympic 100m champion. Split CHAPLIN; the LIN left over begins the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Linford Christie was a British sprinter, an athlete famous for winning Olympic gold.

clue.text: Clap Purviance, unevenly acting like a goat

indicators.note: unevenly takes the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Applaud Edna Purviance, whose acting was patchy, like a goat's.
explanation.walkthrough: Edna Purviance was Chaplin's regular leading lady. Take the first, third, fifth letters and so on of CLAP PURVIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprine means relating to or like goats, from Latin capra, a she-goat.
